body.translated_text: Chapter 1. The Fruits of <s>Nakṣatra</s> (Lunar Mansion) Actions

children.translated_text: The lord of the three worlds, the eye of the universe, dispeller of dense darkness, lion among serpents,
crowned by the mountains of rising and setting, victorious is the Sun, the sole ornament of the sky!

children.text: mūrdhnā gaṇeśaṃ ca sarasvatīṃ ca salokapālaṃ parameśvaraṃ ca/
children.translated_text: With bowed head, I salute <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) together with the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World Guardians),

children.text: padmodbhavaṃ padmadhanaṃ hariṃ ca trailokyadīpaṃ praṇamāmi bhānum//
children.translated_text: <s>Padmodbhava</s> (Brahmā, born from the lotus), <s>Padmadhana</s> (Lakṣmī, whose wealth is the lotus), <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), and <s>Bhānu</s> (the Sun), the lamp of the three worlds!
Henceforth, the procedure of military expedition (<s>yātrā</s>) for one who desires victory, whose birth-time is known,
and whose happiness and misery are determined as divided by year, month, and day:
When the <s>horā</s> (hour) and <s>rāśi</s> (zodiac sign) are known, and the positional strength of the planets is grasped,

children.text: āyuṣi ca parijñāte śubham aśubhaṃ vā phalaṃ vācyam//
children.translated_text: and when the lifespan has been ascertained, the result — auspicious or inauspicious — should be declared.
The instruction of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) applies when the subject matter is thus established with a relevant contradiction;

children.text: janmasamayaṃ ca kecid vadanti na vadanti bahuvo 'nye//
children.translated_text: some declare the birth-time, while many others do not.

children.text: janmarkṣodayalagne tad api yayor vā yiyāsataḥ praśne/
children.translated_text: In the birth <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), the rising <s>lagna</s> (ascendant), or in the query of one who wishes to march, concerning whichever two [of these],
victory shall be in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th positions and in the routes where [favorable signs are] rising overhead.

children.text: śatror horārāśis tad adhipatir janmabhaṃ tadīśo vā//
children.translated_text: If the <s>horā</s> sign of the enemy, its lord, the birth <s>nakṣatra</s>, or its lord

children.text: yady aste hibuke vā tathāpi śatrur hato vācyaḥ//
children.translated_text: is setting or in the 4th house, then too the enemy should be declared defeated.
At the time of the query, if the ground is pleasant and auspicious objects are seen, that is commendable;

children.text: yadi cādareṇa pṛcchati daivajño nirdiśed vijayam//
children.translated_text: and if one asks with respect, the astrologer should predict victory.

children.text: nandā bhadrā vijayā riktā pūrṇā ca nāmasadṛśaphalāḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s> (Joyful), <s>Bhadrā</s> (Auspicious), <s>Vijayā</s> (Victorious), <s>Riktā</s> (Empty), and <s>Pūrṇā</s> (Full) — these <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) give results matching their names;

children.text: nyūnasameṣṭā daśame tithayaḥ śukle kṛṣṇe pratīpās tāḥ//
children.translated_text: in the bright fortnight (<s>śukla</s>), [they are] deficient, equal, and desired on the tenth; in the dark fortnight (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), they are reversed.
A <s>nakṣatra</s> capsule without rays, set in the evening twilight, split by planets,
afflicted by malefics, or vitiated by portents — all [such conditions are] inauspicious.
<s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Maghā</s> (Pitrya), <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Kṛttikā</s>
are not very auspicious for a march; the remaining <s>nakṣatras</s> are auspicious.
For one wishing to burn the enemy's territory, the <s>Āgneyī</s> (fire-related <s>nakṣatra</s>) is auspicious at sunrise except in another case;
not in the <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, or <s>Uttara</s> [group], in the forenoon of the day.
In <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Ārdrā</s> (Raudra), midday should be avoided;
in <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Hasta</s>, the march should be avoided in the afternoon.
In <s>Anurādhā</s> (Maitra), <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s> (Aindava), <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Revatī</s>, one should march after avoiding the early evening;

children.text: pūrveṣu triṣu yāmye pitrye ca vihāya madhyaniśam//
children.translated_text: in the first three of the southern group and in the <s>Pitrya</s> (ancestral), the middle of the night should be avoided.

children.text: na niśāpaścimabhāge punarvasau triṣu ca vaiṣṇavādyeṣu/
children.translated_text: Not in the last part of the night for <s>Punarvasu</s> and the three [nakṣatras] beginning with <s>Śravaṇa</s> (Vaiṣṇava);
all times are auspicious in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> (Aindra), <s>Hasta</s> (Savitra), and <s>Puṣya</s>.

children.text: prācyādi sapta sapta kramena dhiṣṇyāni kṛttikādīni/
children.translated_text: Seven <s>nakṣatras</s> each, beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, in order, [rule] the eastern and other [directions];
in sequence, with unity between the northeast and <s>Śravaṇa</s> and <s>Uttarā</s>.
Those who march crossing the line called <s>Parigha</s> (Obstacle), [running through] the directions of fire and wind,

children.text: ājñām iva kuliśabhṛtaḥ patanti na cireṇa te vyasane//
children.translated_text: as if violating the command of the thunderbolt-bearer (<s>Indra</s>), fall into calamity before long.
A group of four <s>nakṣatras</s> designated as 'all-directional' (<s>sarvadvārika</s>) is specified:
<s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Mitra</s> (Anurādhā).

children.text: jyeṣṭhā prāgbhādrapadā rohiṇy athottarā ca phalgunyā/
children.translated_text: <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>

children.text: śūlāni prācyādiṣu teṣu gato 'tyeti yadi citram//
children.translated_text: are the <s>śūlas</s> (spears) in the eastern and other directions; if one goes in those [directions under those stars], it is a wonder if one survives.

The stars [in relation to the birth star] are: birth (<s>janma</s>), wealth (<s>sampat</s>), danger (<s>vipat</s>), welfare (<s>kṣema</s>), loss (<s>apāya</s>), auspicious (<s>śubha</s>), hardship (<s>kaṣṭa</s>),
friendly (<s>maitra</s>), and extremely friendly (<s>atimaitra</s>) — these give results corresponding to their names.
Chapter 2. The Fruits of the Day-Lord (<s>Dineśa</s>)
On Sunday, loss of wealth; on Monday, loss of strength and loss of food;
on Tuesday, fever, blood [disorders], and bilious diseases; on Wednesday, acquisition of friends.
On Thursday (<s>Jīva</s>), victory and gain of wealth; on Friday (<s>Śukra</s>), gain of women, clothes, perfumes, and wealth;
on Saturday (day of the son of the Sun), one suffers misery, imprisonment, and diseases.
On the day when the planet occupying the <s>upacaya</s> (growth) house is [lord], success comes to the marcher even if [the planet is] malefic;

children.text: saumye 'py anupacayasthe na bhavati yātrā śubhā yātuḥ//E3
children.translated_text: even if a benefic is not in the <s>upacaya</s> position, the march is not auspicious for the traveler.
Chapter 3. The Qualities of <s>Muhūrta</s> (Auspicious Moment) Actions
The <s>karaṇas</s> (half-days) excluding <s>Gara</s>, <s>Vaṇij</s>, and <s>Viṣṭi</s> (Bhadrā) are desirable for the marcher;

children.text: garam api kaiś cic chastaṃ vaṇijā(jāṃ) ca vaṇikkriyāsv eva//
children.translated_text: though <s>Gara</s> is commended by some, and <s>Vaṇij</s> only for mercantile activities.
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Bhujaga</s> (Serpent), <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Pitṛ</s> (Ancestor), <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Jala</s> (Water), <s>Viśva</s> (All-Gods), <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), and <s>Paṅkajaprabha</s> (Lotus-Born)
are [the deities of the <s>muhūrtas</s>]; <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, another <s>Indra</s>, <s>Niśācara</s> (Night-Wanderer), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Yoni</s> (Source) during the day;
<s>Rudra</s>, <s>Aja</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Antaka</s> (Death), <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>,
<s>Indu</s> (Moon), <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Anila</s> (Wind) — these are the <s>muhūrtas</s> of the night.

children.text: ahnaḥ pañcadaśāṃśo rātreś caivaṃ muhūrta iti saṃjñā/
children.translated_text: A <s>muhūrta</s> is defined as one-fifteenth of the day and likewise of the night;

children.text: sa ca vijñeyas tajjñaiś chāyāyantrāmbubhir yuktyā//
children.translated_text: it should be determined by experts through shadow-instruments, water-clocks, and calculation.

children.text: nakṣatravat kṣaṇānāṃ parighādi tadīśvaraiḥ samaṃ cintyam/
children.translated_text: Like <s>nakṣatras</s>, the <s>parigha</s> (obstacle) and other [factors] of the <s>muhūrtas</s> should be considered together with their lords;

children.text: phalam api tad eva dṛṣṭaṃ gargādyais tatra ca ślokāḥ//
children.translated_text: the same results have been observed by <s>Garga</s> and others; and there are verses on this:
A complete day-and-night, conjoined with the lunar <s>nakṣatra</s>,
[yields] <s>nakṣatra-muhūrtas</s> that are declared to have the same action-qualities.

children.text: yaś cāṣṭamo muhūrto viriñcināmābhijit sa nirdiṣṭaḥ/
children.translated_text: The eighth <s>muhūrta</s>, named <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), is designated <s>Abhijit</s>;
in that [muhūrta]... in the southern direction, victory is gained by one who has gone to the extreme.

children.text: aṣṭamena divase same śubho yo viriñcivibhusaṃjñitāḥ(taḥ)(add.kṣaṇaḥ)/
children.translated_text: On the eighth day, in an even [position], the auspicious <s>muhūrta</s> designated by the names <s>Viriñci</s> and <s>Vibhu</s>,
by that [muhūrta], a march avoiding the southern [direction] is praised in all directions — [this is] <s>Abhijit</s>.
Chapter 4. The Fruits of the Moon (<s>Candra</s>)
The Moon in the <s>upacaya</s> (growth) houses or the seventh is auspicious for a march, even in the birth <s>nakṣatra</s>;
if conjoined with a benefic producing success, in an auspicious [sign], the result is auspicious.
The Moon in the 1st (birth), 3rd, 6th, 11th, or 7th is not recommended;
in the 5th, 9th, last (12th), 8th, 4th, or 2nd, the results are of desired fruit according to distinctions.

children.text: sitapakṣādau candre śubhe śubhaṃ pakṣam aśubham aśubhe ca/
children.translated_text: When the Moon is auspicious at the beginning of the bright fortnight, the fortnight is auspicious; when inauspicious, inauspicious;

children.text: kṛṣṇe gocaraśubhado na śubhaṃ pakṣa(kṣe) śubham atonyat//E3
children.translated_text: in the dark fortnight, if [the Moon] gives auspicious transit results, the fortnight is not auspicious — the reverse applies.
Chapter 5. Purification of the <s>Lagna</s> (Ascendant)

children.text: iṣṭaṃ svajanmalagnaṃ na janmarāśyudgamas tayoḥ sthānāt/
children.translated_text: One's own birth <s>lagna</s> is desired; not the rising of the birth <s>rāśi</s> (zodiac sign); from the position of those two,
the 3rd, 11th houses... are beneficial at rising; the rest are undesired.
If the enemy's 8th house [is rising], the enemy is slain; if the enemy's 6th [is] at the <s>lagna</s>, the marcher is slain;
some say likewise when the Sun is in the enemy's... cruel [position].

children.text: āye janmani rāśiṣu yeṣu śubhā bhāskaradvitīyai//
children.translated_text: In which <s>rāśis</s> the Sun and others are auspicious at the 11th, the birth, [and other houses],
those are commended at the <s>lagna</s>; malefic planets are not desired...
In head-rising [signs], victory; in tail-rising [signs] at the <s>lagna</s>, defeat;
in direction-[compatible signs], victory; in door-[signs], defeat in battle.
In <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces), the path is crooked; even if that... Moon <s>lagna</s> [applies],
a water-journey should be undertaken with an aquatic <s>lagna</s> or in its <s>navāṃśa</s> (ninth division).
Chapter 6. Divisions of the <s>Lagna</s>
In the Moon's <s>nakṣatra</s>, the <s>navāṃśas</s> with malefics...
like the frivolities of youth by a wise man in the final days [should be avoided].
Prosperity comes for one wishing to march when benefic planets are in the <s>navāṃśa lagna</s>,
like traversing the wilderness of youth, having relied upon skill by the righteous.
When a benefic is in the <s>navāṃśa</s> of the <s>lagna</s>, it makes the enemy's power and enjoyments irresistible;
whatever fruit [comes] on those days, all of that [also applies] in the <s>kālahorā</s> (time-hour).
The <s>varga</s> (division) of even a malefic planet occupying the <s>upacaya</s> (growth) house is praised at the <s>lagna</s>;
when the Moon is in a foot-conjunction... of the benefic lord of the <s>tantra</s> (chart).
Thus, malefics in the 8th should be avoided; the 8th <s>lagna</s> [should be avoided] as well,
and the Moon... in the 8th house, in all undertakings and activities.
A march without [consideration of] the <s>lagna</s> is like a deranged woman;
encountering someone hard to know, she gradually goes to ruin.
A march governed by the <s>lagna</s>, like a well-born woman by her character,
brings about [good] fortune and... qualities and beauty of the highest [order].
Chapter 7. Purification of the Planets (<s>Grahaviśuddhi</s>)

children.text: lagnopagataiḥ saumyair ārogyaṃ bhavati cittasaukhyañ ca/
children.translated_text: With benefics at the <s>lagna</s>, there is health and mental happiness;
with them in the 2nd house, accumulation of wealth; in the 3rd, increase of the army.

children.text: vāhanasuhṛdāṃ vṛddhiś caturthagaiḥ pañcagaiś ca mantribalam/
children.translated_text: With them in the 4th, increase of vehicles and friends; in the 5th, strength of ministers;
in the 6th, destruction of enemies; except for <s>Venus</s>, those in the 7th are beneficial.
They protect in the 8th house of longevity; except for the Moon in the 9th, [there is] acquisition of wealth;

children.text: karmaṇi siddhir lābho balasampātaś ca daśamādyaiḥ//
children.translated_text: success in the 10th (house of action), gain, and encounter with strength [come from planets] in the 10th and other [houses].
With <s>Mars</s>, the Sun, <s>Saturn</s>, and the Moon at the <s>lagna</s>, [there are] killing, imprisonment, death, and terror;
in the 2nd, loss of wealth; in the 3rd, luminous fame.
Separation from vehicles and kinsmen, failure of counsel, destruction of enemies —
in the 4th and other [houses]; in the 7th, destruction of one's own territory; and with <s>Venus</s> [in the 7th],
death from [malefics] at the 8th house; great disaster to the army from those in the 9th;
<s>Mars</s> and the Sun in the 10th give victory; <s>Saturn</s> gives defeat.
Malefics in the 11th give victory; in the 12th, breaking of one's own forces;
except in <s>upacaya</s> houses, benefics [are favorable] for the marcher; malefics [give] the reverse.

children.text: krūro 'py anukūlasthaḥ śasto lagne śubho 'pi vāniṣṭaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even a malefic in a favorable position is commended at the <s>lagna</s>; even a benefic in an unfavorable position is not desired;

children.text: vakrī na śubhaḥ kendre tadahas tadvargalagnañ ca//
children.translated_text: a retrograde [planet] is not auspicious in an angle (<s>kendra</s>); on that day, [avoid] that <s>varga</s> (division) <s>lagna</s> also.
<s>Jupiter</s> and the Moon are [lords] of alliance; <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, <s>Mercury</s>, and <s>Saturn</s> are [lords] of discord;
<s>Sun</s> and <s>Mars</s> are of punishment; and <s>Mercury</s>, then the Moon, of gift-giving.
Forest-dwellers, territorial [lords], enemies, ministers, crown-princes, guild-leaders, mercenaries, and valiant lords —

children.text: sūryādibhir anukūlais tad udayavargaiś ca tatsiddhiḥ//
children.translated_text: their success [is determined] by the favorable [positions] of the Sun and other [planets] and by the groups [of planets] at their rising.
Planets that are in their fall, defeated [in planetary war], overpowered by the Sun, deprived of rays, and diminished —

children.text: bhujagā iva mantrahatā bhavanty akāryakṣamā lagne//
children.translated_text: like serpents struck by <s>mantras</s> (sacred incantations), they become incapable of producing results in the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant).

children.text: yeṣāṃ game navamapañcamakaṇṭakasthāḥ saumyās trītīyaripulābhagatāś ca pāpāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those for whom benefic planets are in the ninth, fifth, and angular positions, and malefic planets are in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses —

children.text: āyānti te svabhavanāni punaḥ kṛtārthāḥ dattā dvijātiṣu tathā vidhivad yathārthāḥ//
children.translated_text: they return to their own homes having accomplished their purpose, like gifts properly given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (twice-born) according to the rites and their true value.

children.text: ekasminn api kendre yadi saumyo na graho 'sti yātrāyām/
children.translated_text: If not even a single benefic planet is in an angle (<s>kendra</s>) during the military expedition,

children.text: janmany atha vā karmaṇi na tac chubhaṃ prāhur ācāryāḥ//
children.translated_text: or in the nativity, or in the action [chart] — the teachers declare that it is not auspicious.
<s>Rāhu</s>, the Sun, <s>Mars</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and the Moon are travelers (<s>yāyins</s>); the Moon is also the crier (<s>ākranda</s>);
<s>Jupiter</s>, <s>Mercury</s>, and <s>Saturn</s> are sedentary (<s>pauras</s>); the Sun also is sedentary in the forenoon.

children.text: yāyibhir anukūlasthair yānaṃ paurair vigṛhya cāsīnam/
children.translated_text: With travelers favorably placed, one should march; with sedentary [planets], one should remain seated and engaged;

children.text: pauretarair api śubhair yāyād ardhena sainyasya//
children.translated_text: even with other [planets that are] auspicious being travelers, one should march with half the army.

children.text: sarvair apy aśubhakaraiḥ śubhadaivaṃ saṃśrayet pradhānanṛpam/
children.translated_text: Even when all [planets] produce inauspicious [results], one should resort to a chief king of auspicious destiny;

children.text: balasiddhiḥ saumyaphalair balibhiḥ krūrair jayo yuddhe//E16
children.translated_text: success of the army [comes] from benefic planets that are strong; victory in battle [comes] from malefic planets that are powerful.
Chapter 8: Concordance of Directional Planets
Movement concordant with the course (<s>ayana</s>) is beneficial; when both the Sun and Moon are unfavorable,
one should march day and night for victory; in the opposite case, there is distress, defeat, and slaughter.

children.text: udito yato yataś ca bhramaṇe yadvārabheṣu cāragate/
children.translated_text: From where [the Sun] has risen and from where [Venus] is in transit, at the commencement of which [planetary] period —
that threefold [direction] opposite to <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) should be avoided; there one should make an effort [only] at the rising.

children.text: na pratiśukre siddhiṃ svalpo 'py arthaḥ prayāti yātṛṇām/
children.translated_text: Not even the slightest purpose of travelers succeeds [when marching] against <s>Śukra</s> (Venus);

children.text: kāmaṃ vrajet pratibhṛguṃ jijīviṣur nāstage śukre//
children.translated_text: one may indeed march against <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) if one wishes to live, but never when <s>Śukra</s> is set.

children.text: kaluṣi vapuṣi grahahate pratilome nīcage 'stage ca bhṛgau/
children.translated_text: When <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus) is turbid in body, afflicted by planets, retrograde, in its fall, or set,

children.text: balasaṃpanno 'pi nṛpo yātā śatror vaśaṃ yāti//
children.translated_text: even a king endowed with strength, if he marches, comes under the power of his enemy.
[On the forehead, [Venus] causes fear of fire; the Sun causes depletion of the treasury; Mars [causes]
[victory over enemies; the son of the Moon (Mercury) [causes] disruption of the army; <s>Jupiter</s> [causes]
[death; the son of the Sun (Saturn) [causes] destruction of warriors; the king of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (Jupiter) [causes]
[all of these combined; the lord of demons' minister, the bull, [is] <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus).

children.text: [nakṣatraṃ tithi(tha)yas tathaiva karaṇaṃ vāras tathā gocaraṃ
children.translated_text: [The <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), <s>karaṇa</s> (half-lunar day), weekday, and <s>gocara</s> (planetary transit),
[the <s>drekkāṇa</s> (decanate), with the <s>navāṃśa</s> (ninth-part division), planetary day, the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant), and the <s>muhūrta</s> (auspicious moment) —

children.text: [ye cānye śakunādayo nigaditāḥ sarve 'pi te śobhanā
children.translated_text: [and whatever other omens such as bird-signs are declared — all of these are auspicious
[on the forehead of the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus); at that time not even <s>Indra</s> [can prevail] against <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter).
[Even a god he would conquer, having placed <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) behind him,
[the king who, thirsting for victory in battle, sets forth;
[having satiated the earth with the streams of blood of the enemy's forces,
[he enjoys widespread and great fame for a long time.

children.text: [naur iva vikarṇadharā vi(lacuna)(dha)veda vadhūr vibhāskareva dyauḥ/
children.translated_text: [Like a boat without a rudder, like... like a wife without the brilliant one (the Sun), like the sky [without light],
[like the earth with ruined crops — so is an expedition when <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) has departed.
Even in such a [condition] of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), one may march if the son of the Moon (<s>Mercury</s>) is favorably placed;
other planets are not capable of protecting one who marches against <s>Mercury</s> (Budha).

children.text: yo 'pi patir diśi yasyāṃ tasmin tatsthe na tāṃ diśaṃ yāyāt/
children.translated_text: Whoever is the lord of a particular direction — when [a malefic] is stationed in that [direction], one should not march in that direction;
when the directional lord is favorable, one should march, even when an afflicting planet occupies it.
Chapter 9.
On days of <s>Vyatīpāta</s>, <s>Viṣṭi</s> (Bhadrā), <s>Vaidhṛti</s>, malefic planetary <s>lagnas</s> (ascendants), and [unfavorable] planetary groups,
theft, ambush, falsehood, and battle do not succeed.

children.text: hutvānalaṃ namaskṛtya devatāḥ svasti vācya viprāṃś ca/
children.translated_text: Having offered oblations into the fire, having saluted the deities, having pronounced blessings upon the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: dhyāyan digīśam avilambitaṃ vrajed bhūpatiḥ sumanāḥ//
children.translated_text: meditating on the lord of the direction, the king should set forth without delay, with a cheerful mind.

children.text: kāryavaśāt svayam agamaṃ bhūbhartuḥ kecid āhur ācāryāḥ/
children.translated_text: Some teachers say that the king's departure should be [determined] by the exigency of the task itself;
at the time of departure, he should perform the victory rite with umbrella, weapons, and the like.
One should not [march] at all during untimely rain, lightning, or thunder, deeming it inauspicious,
nor for seven days after celestial, atmospheric, or terrestrial portents.

children.text: dakṣiṇapārśvaspandanam iṣṭaṃ hṛdayaṃ vihāya pṛṣṭhaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: Throbbing of the right side is auspicious, [but] not of the heart or the back;

children.text: manasaś cāgamaśuddhiḥ ślokaś cāyaṃ munibhir uktaḥ//
children.translated_text: and the purity of the mind [should be ascertained] at departure — and this verse has been spoken by the sages:
'Let all the omens, whether auspicious or inauspicious, be on one side;

children.text: ekataś ca mano yāti tad viśuddhaṃ jayāvaham//
children.translated_text: and on the other side stands the mind — when that is pure, it brings victory.'

children.text: ārohati kṣitipatau vinayopapanno yātrānugo 'nyaturagaṃ pratiheṣitaś ca/
children.translated_text: When the lord of the earth mounts [his horse] and the horse, submissive and accompanying the march, neighs in response to another horse,

children.text: vaktreṇa vā spṛśati dakṣiṇam ātmapārśvaṃ yo 'śvaḥ sa bhartur acirāt pracinoti lakṣmīm//
children.translated_text: or touches with its mouth the right flank of its own body — such a horse quickly brings prosperity to its master.

children.text: muhurmuhur mūtraśakṛt karoti na tāḍyamāno 'py anulomayāyī/
children.translated_text: A horse that frequently passes urine and dung, that does not move forward even when struck,

children.text: akāryabhīto 'śruvilocanaś ca śivaṃ na bhartus turago 'bhidhatte//
children.translated_text: that is frightened of the task [ahead] and has tearful eyes — such a horse does not bring welfare to its master.

children.text: skhalitagatir akasmāt trastakarṇo 'tidīnaḥ śvasati mṛdu sudīrghaṃ nyastahastaḥ pṛthivyām/
children.translated_text: One that stumbles in gait, suddenly has startled ears, appears greatly dejected, breathes softly and deeply, places its forefoot upon the ground,

children.text: drutamukulitadṛṣṭiḥ svapnaśīlo vikomo bhayakṛd ahitabhakṣī naikaśo 'sṛkśakṛtkṛt//
children.translated_text: quickly closes its eyes, is drowsy, disobedient, fear-inspiring, eats harmful things, and repeatedly produces blood and dung [from its body] —
one that uproots anthills, stumps, bushes, grass, and trees, with joyful eyes of its own accord,

children.text: yāyād yātrānulomaṃ tvaritapadagatir vaktram unnamya coccaiḥ/
children.translated_text: should march in the direction of the expedition, with swift pace, lifting its face upward and neighing loudly.
At the time of saddling and harnessing, if [the horse] produces great foam or shakes itself,

children.text: tatkālaṃ vā madāptau jayakṛd atha radaṃ veṣṭayan dakṣiṇaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: or at that very time enters a state of rut — it is victory-bringing; also [if] it wraps its bit to the right side.
White mustard, mirrors, milk, ointments, a tethered animal, meat, and full water-jars;
turbans, water-pots, men of distinction, chariots, <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), and parasols;
curds, honey, ghee, yellow pigment (<s>rocanā</s>), maidens, banners, gold, lotuses, auspicious seats, and conch-shells;
white bulls, flowers, garments, fish, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, courtesans, kinsmen, and people in fine attire;
blazing fires, fruits, unbroken rice, sugarcane, food-offerings, elephants, drums, goads, <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), and weapons;
emeralds, rubies, <s>padmarāga</s> (rubies/tourmalines), crystals, and the foremost varieties of gems —

children.text: svayam atha racitāny ayatnato vā yadi kathitāni bhavanti maṅgalāni/
children.translated_text: if these auspicious [objects] appear, whether arranged deliberately or spontaneously,

children.text: sa jayati sakalāṃ tato dharitrīṃ grahaṇadṛgālabhanaśrutair upāsya//
children.translated_text: that [king] conquers the entire earth thereby, worshipping them by grasping, gazing, touching, and hearing.
Cotton, herbs, black grain, salt, eunuchs, bones, oil, fat,
mud, charcoal, molasses, snake-skins, and dung — [these] cause distress, along with the sick;
the intoxicated, the insane, the stupefied, the blind, the deaf, the hungry, the emaciated, the bitter, and enemies;
the tonsured, the anointed, the disheveled, the fallen, and those wearing saffron robes — [all these are] inauspicious.
One should proceed along a road [resounding with] clear drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, conch-shells, kettledrums, and the din of musical instruments, with raised banners and arches at its entrance,
abundant with flowers and water, with dust settled, fragrant, and filled with well-dressed people.
Whatever auspicious and inauspicious [omens] are taught here for those setting out,

children.text: svapneṣv api tāni śubhāśubhāni viḍlepanaṃ dhanyam//
children.translated_text: those same [apply as] auspicious and inauspicious in dreams as well; anointing with cow-dung is auspicious.

children.text: mṛdur anukūlaḥ snigdhapavanaḥ tadvad vīnā(ṇā)ś ca śasyante/
children.translated_text: A soft, favorable, and moist breeze, and likewise <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), are praised;

children.text: lalāṭaṃ dhanur athendraṃ(nuraindraṃ)na śubhadam anyatra śastaṃ(sta)phalam//
children.translated_text: a rainbow on the forehead is not auspicious, but elsewhere [its] fruit is praiseworthy.
A male-named [animal], a house-lizard (<s>gṛhagodhikā</s>), a tawny [animal], a jackal, a dark [animal],
a cuckoo, a female pig, and a <s>ralā</s> — on the left side when setting forth, [these are] praised.
Female-named [animals], a <s>bhāsa</s> (vulture), a <s>bhaṣa</s>, a <s>kapiñjala</s> (francolin partridge), a diver, a <s>kambuka</s>, a <s>kiṃtsaka</s>,
a peacock, a <s>śrīkaṣṭha</s>, a <s>pippīka</s>, a <s>ruru</s> deer, and a hawk — [these are auspicious] on the right side.
The sight of a <s>bhāradvāja</s> bird, a peacock, a snake, and a mongoose is auspicious;
the [sight of] a monitor lizard, a snake, a <s>jāhaka</s>, a chameleon, and a hare gives inauspicious results.
The cry of a crow, a hare, a monitor lizard, a snake, and a pig is desired [as auspicious];
but their sight is inauspicious — the opposite [applies] for monkeys and bears.

children.text: mṛgavihagā śasyante pradakṣiṇaṃ viṣamasaṃkhyayā ca mṛgāḥ/
children.translated_text: Animals and birds are praised [when seen] moving clockwise and in odd numbers;
at the time of a king's appearance for departure, the same [applies]; but the opposite [applies] at the time of entry.
One who is given to insult, injurious to men, with disaffected servants, an adulterer,
greedy, without allies, addicted to vices, ungrateful, a violator of established order, with a kingdom crumbling under taxation;

children.text: visrambhahā krodhavaśe(śo) nṛśaṃse(saḥ) kṣudrā(draḥ) pramādī na bahuśrutā(ta)ś ca/
children.translated_text: a betrayer of trust, subject to anger, cruel, petty, negligent, and unlearned —

children.text: divyāntarikṣakṣitijau(jai)r vikārair nipīḍito (yaś ca) sa daivahīnaḥ//
children.translated_text: one who is afflicted by celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial disturbances — such [a king] is bereft of fate (<s>daiva</s>).

children.text: ato viparyastaguṇena rājñā tādṛgvidho 'ris tv abhiyuktamātraḥ/
children.translated_text: When attacked even [but slightly] by an enemy with qualities the opposite [of these], such a [fate-bereft king],

children.text: tarur ghuṇair jagdha ivāttakāryo mahān api kṣipram upaiti bhaṅgāḥ(ṅgam)//
children.translated_text: like a tree eaten away by termites, even if great, quickly meets his ruin.
An army bereft of excellent heroic men's valor, lacking courage, deprived of fine elephants, horses, and warriors,
accompanied by portents, reversals of natural order, and affliction-laden grief, quickly [succumbs to] the enemy's forces.

children.text: saṃgrāme va(ya)m amara(dvija)prasādā(t) jyeṣyāmo ripubalam āśv asaṃśayena/
children.translated_text: 'In battle, by the grace of the gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, we shall swiftly conquer the enemy's forces without doubt' —

children.text: yasye(syai)vaṃ bhavati bale janapravādāḥ(daḥ) svalpo 'pi pravarabalaṃ nihanti rājā//
children.translated_text: when such talk arises among the people regarding an army, even a small king destroys a superior force.
The lord of the earth should destroy the city of the enemy when the enemy is afflicted by inauspicious planets and unfavorable <s>diṅniviṣṭi</s> (directional omens).

children.text: yuddhasya yātrāsama eva kālaḥ kū(krū)reṣu lagneṣu ca kūṭāyudhaḥ(kūṭayuddhaṃ)//
children.translated_text: The time for battle is the same as for the military march; and when the ascendant is in cruel signs, deceptive warfare is indicated.
Birds stationed on the ramparts, facing inward, announce danger to the citizens;

children.text: āgantunāśāya bahirmukhās te tulyaṃ vihaṅgaiḥ saramātmajau(jā)ś ca//
children.translated_text: those facing outward announce destruction of the invader; the same applies to dogs and their offspring as to birds.
When <s>Ketu</s>, meteors, <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Kīlaka</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) enter the disk of the Sun or Moon from a certain direction,

children.text: sūryendvoḥ pariveṣakhaṇḍam athavā dṛśyeta yasyāṃ diśi/
children.translated_text: or when a segment of the halo of the Sun or Moon is seen in whatever direction,
or when jackals, dogs, bees, ants, hares, deer, crows, and other creatures enter the city

children.text: sainye vāpi yato viśanti hi tataḥ śatro(troḥ) puraṃ ghātayet//
children.translated_text: or the army—from whatever direction they enter, from that direction one should destroy the enemy's city.

children.text: pātālarkṣe rāhuketvo(tvoḥ) pure 'reto(s to)yocchittiḥ sālapātaś ca kāryaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s> are in the subterranean <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), the water supply to the city should be cut off and trees should be felled;

children.text: jāmitrasthe bhūmijā(je ')syāṃśake vā putreṇendor vīkṣite 'gniḥ pradeyaḥ//
children.translated_text: when <s>Bhūmija</s> (Mars) is in the seventh house or its division, or when aspected by <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter, son of the Moon), fire should be employed.
Upon acquiring the city in an enemy's territory, the king should not oppress
virtuous people, temples, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, noble families, and women;
and he should not kill those without elephants, horses, and weapons, nor the afflicted and frightened;
he should enter the conquered city on an auspicious <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), day, and <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), with his army joyful.
Through portents such as the burning of a direction, shooting stars, dust, showers of stones,

children.text: yuddhānte mṛgaśakunaiś ca dīptanādaiḥ no bhadraṃ bhavati jite pari('pi) pārthivasya//
children.translated_text: thunderclaps, earthquakes, and other disturbances, and through animals and birds with blazing cries at the end of battle—there is no good fortune for the king, even in victory.
When animals and birds are auspicious, the breezes are gentle and comforting,
the planets have bright rays, and the sky is free from dust—

children.text: yad anyam a(da)pi vikṛtai(taṃ) na vijayāvasāne bhavet
children.translated_text: when no other disturbance or portent occurs at the conclusion of victory,

children.text: tadā sukham akaṇṭakaṃ nṛpatir atti deśe ripuḥ(ripoḥ)//E35
children.translated_text: then the king enjoys the enemy's territory in happiness and without obstruction.
